primary.title: Memoirs of Catherine the Great
primary.author: Catherine II of Russia
primary.rationale: Catherine's personal memoirs offer direct insight into her thoughts, experiences, and perspective on her rise to power and reign. These are widely considered a foundational primary source for her biography.

primary.title: The Correspondence of Catherine the Great
primary.author: Catherine II of Russia
primary.rationale: Her extensive correspondence with prominent figures of her time (e.g., Voltaire, Diderot, Frederick the Great) reveals her intellectual engagement, political strategies, and personal opinions on a wide range of topics.

primary.title: Nakaz (Instruction) of Catherine the Great
primary.author: Catherine II of Russia
primary.rationale: This document outlines Catherine's legislative program and her vision for the reform of Russian law, drawing heavily on Enlightenment ideas. It is a key primary source for understanding her political and philosophical aims.

secondary.title: Catherine the Great: Portrait of a Woman
secondary.author: Robert K. Massie
secondary.rationale: A highly acclaimed and comprehensive biography by a Pulitzer Prize-winning historian, offering a detailed and nuanced portrait of Catherine's life, reign, and impact.

secondary.title: Catherine the Great: A Short Biography
secondary.author: Isabel de Madariaga
secondary.rationale: A concise yet authoritative scholarly overview of Catherine's reign by a leading historian of Russia, focusing on her political achievements and the complexities of her rule.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to the Age of Catherine the Great
secondary.author: David Griffiths
secondary.rationale: This edited volume brings together essays by various scholars on different aspects of Catherine's era, providing diverse scholarly perspectives on her reign, policies, and cultural impact.

suggestions.notes: Primary source dates reflect the period of writing or publication, not necessarily the earliest available editions. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly reputation and recency.
